title: GPU fragility stressbench for sliced KV-cache and activation slotting
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: We need a reproducible stress benchmark that exposes GPU-level fragility across the three primary memory consumers (weights, KV cache, activations) under continuous batching. The goal is to quantify failure modes (OOM, preemption-induced latency spikes, cross-tenant interference) for sliced KV layouts and activation slotting strategies and to produce a headroom guidance model for runtime autoscalers.
acceptance_criteria: A benchmark harness that can simulate mixed-length request traces at configurable QPS and batch windows
Clear breakdown of memory footprint per-GPU into weights | kv | activations | ephemeral (strings, temp buffers) under representative runs
Quantified OOM/probability curves for at least three KV fragmentation strategies (monolithic, slab-sliced, slot-compact) across 2 model sizes
Headroom model (CSV) that maps target p95 latency + target OOM rate -> recommended soft-margin percentage and preemption slab size
Two recommended runtime mitigations implemented as patch prototypes: a) soft-eviction watermark that prioritizes inactive KV slots, b) prefaulted activation buffers for steady-state batching
Benchmark results published to benchmarks.redwood.internal with dashboards and linked PRs
technical_approach: Create a lightweight harness (python + rust microbench) that drives the runtime via the same RPC path as production to avoid synthetic kernel bypass
Instrument GPU memory accounting hooks in the serving runtime to emit per-component telemetry (weights, kv_slots_used, kv_slots_reserved, activation_bytes_live, ephemeral_bytes)
Implement three KV-layout variants behind an abstract interface so the benchmark can flip strategies at runtime: monolithic, slab-sliced, slot-compact
Simulate continuous-batching patterns: steady QPS, bursty QPS, and adversarial interleaving of long-short sequences
Run experiments on two GPU profiles (A100-40GB and H100-80GB) and three model families (7B, 13B, 70B quantized where applicable)
Build a headroom estimator that fits a probabilistic model (Weibull/GPD) to OOM/eviction events and outputs recommended margin percentiles
Validate estimator with k-fold stress runs and report confidence intervals
experiment_plan: Week 1: Harness + telemetry hooks; smoke runs against a single model on dev cluster
Week 2: Implement KV-layout variants + activation slotting toggle; run matrix against A100 dev nodes
Week 3: Repeat matrix on H100 and collect distributional stats; tune eviction heuristics
Week 4: Finalize headroom estimator, generate dashboard, author RFC for runtime changes and rollout plan
metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency under continuous batching
GPU utilization (SM and memory) and fragmentation index (free_chunks_stddev / mean)
KV hit ratio and cold-slot eviction frequency
Effective tail latency delta when triggering soft-eviction vs hard-eviction
decisions: Benchmark will use production RPC path to surface realistic kernel/kernel-selection behavior
Prioritize slot-compact layout for prototyping as it is predicted to reduce fragmentation for mixed-length workloads
Headroom guidance will be conservative (favor availability over 5% throughput improvement) for initial rollout
Eviction prototype will be a prioritized LRU over inactive slots rather than bulk purge to avoid quality regressions
tradeoffs: Slot-compact reduces fragmentation but increases CPU bookkeeping; may raise per-request overhead by ~2-4%
Aggressive soft-eviction reduces OOMs but can increase token-level latency for some long sequences when KV-prefetch misses occur
Prefaulting activation buffers lowers latency variance but uses headroom proactively, reducing peak throughput capacity
